For a 50-person company, I’d compare total programme cost, not just airfare. Public TMC pricing is mostly quote-based, so I would not invent a per-booking fee where the provider doesn’t publish one.

What the real annual cost looks like

For your 50-person company, request each vendor to price the same scenario, e.g. ₹50 lakh annual travel spend / 500 bookings:

Total = ₹50L travel spend + booking fees + offline/agent fees + cancellation/amendment fees + payment charges + implementation/integration + GST − negotiated corporate savings.

The biggest hidden-cost difference is usually changes and cancellations, not the initial booking fee.

Terms I would demand before signing

Exact per-ticket/per-hotel fee, including offline bookings.

Cancellation + amendment fee separately from airline/hotel penalties.

24/7 support SLA: response time, escalation and emergency handling.

Refund SLA: when money is received from supplier vs when TMC credits you.

No markup ambiguity: ask whether quoted fare is net, marked-up or commission-inclusive.

Credit terms: ideally monthly invoicing rather than employee reimbursement.

GST invoice guarantee and reconciliation process.

Service-level remedy if support misses the agreed SLA.

Implementation/exit fees and minimum contract period.

Whether corporate-negotiated fares are actually cheaper than public fares after all fees.

For a 50-person company, the most useful RFP is therefore not “what is your subscription price?” but “quote us all-in cost for 500 bookings, including 50 cancellations and 75 changes.” That will expose the actual TCO much faster.
